findings.sentence: In a five-year prospective study of 228 girls (ADHD-combined, n = 93; ADHDinattentive, n = 47; without ADHD, n = 88), Mikami et al. (2008) found that those with a childhood ADHD-combined presentation reported greater adolescent desire to lose weight, assessed using a composite of body dissatisfaction, drive for thinness, and perceived-ideal body-size discrepancy, than girls without ADHD (p <.01, d = 0.63).

Adolescents with persistently elevated inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity reported greater body dissatisfaction and drive for thinness at ages 16-17 years than those with consistently low symptoms (p < .01), including after adjustment for BMI or anxiety/depression symptoms.

Similarly, in a prospective longitudinal community cohort, Bufferd et al. (2022) found that ADHD diagnosis at age 6 was weakly associated with greater body dissatisfaction at age 12 (r = .12, p < .05), but not at age 15.

These findings were consistent across diagnostic subgroups, with no significant associations observed among participants with anorexia nervosa or those with bulimia nervosa, eating disorder not otherwise specified, or binge eating disorder (all ps ≥ .230).

In adjusted regression analyses, sex-neutral body characteristics were associated with ADHD symptoms among participants with Turner syndrome (p <.05), while genital and secondary sex-characteristic satisfaction were associated with ADHD symptoms among female participants with XY-DSD without androgenization (p <.05).

In adjusted regression analyses, sex-neutral body characteristics were associated with ADHD symptoms among participants with Turner syndrome (p <.05), while genital and secondary sex-characteristic satisfaction were associated with ADHD symptoms among female participants with XY-DSD without androgenization (p <.05).

Body image dimensions were also identified as significant individual predictors among female participants with partially androgenized XY-DSD and male participants with XY-DSD (both ps <.05), although the overall regression models for these groups were not statistically significant.

I reviewed replications of six studies where an original claim statistic had p < .01, but the replication produced a significant reverse effect.

papers.title: Tightening Up Under Threat? Reassessing the Link Between Lower Social Class and Cultural Tightness: Comment on Lin et al. (2026)
papers.summary: We found 3 imprecise *p* values out of 26 detected *p* values.

findings.sentence: Household income and personal income were not significantly associated with any of the three outcomes, |r|s ≤ .06, ps ≥ .102.
Education was positively associated with all three outcomes, with rs ranging from .09 to .12 and ps ≤ .011.

Childhood financial condition, the measure of class origin in Study 4, was not significantly associated with any of the three parental tightness outcomes, with rs ranging from -.01 to .06 and ps ≥ .069.
